text:
Several power banks support Qi2.2 25W wireless charging. The 25W speed generally needs an iPhone 16 or newer (not the 16e), and older iPhones get less.

**Available in the US**

- **Anker MagGo 2 Pro (10,000mAh)**: $109.99. It has an active cooling fan, a smart display, a built-in stand and 45W USB-C in/out. It's a pre-order shipping Oct 21 to Nov 9, 2026. [Buy at Anker](https://www.anker.com/products/a110r-qi2-maggo-2-pro-magnetic-power-bank?Sort_by=Recommended&collections_anker-earth-day-sale-2026=&variant=46550444277910)
- **Baseus PicoGo AM52 (10,000mAh)**: Qi2.2 certified with a 45W USB-C port and 30W recharging. Notebookcheck lists it at $79.99 on Amazon US, with a launch price of $59.99 on Baseus's own site. It gets 25W on iPhone 16/17 and 15W on iPhone 12 to 15. Sources: [Notebookcheck](https://www.notebookcheck.net/Baseus-launches-new-Qi2-2-25W-certified-10-000-mAh-power-bank-with-slim-design.1223437.0.html), [Dealectric spec page](https://dealectric.com/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w). I don't have a direct store link for it, so search "Baseus PicoGo AM52" on Amazon or Baseus.com.
- **UGREEN MagFlow 25W**: the first Qi2.2-certified power bank, per [UGREEN's announcement](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/ugreen-pioneers-next-gen-wireless-charging-with-magflow-25w-the-worlds-first-qi-2-2-certified-power-bank-302505385.html). It was slated for Amazon and UGREEN's site. I couldn't confirm current pricing or a product page.
- **ESR MagSlim (10,000mAh)**: 13.8mm thick and billed as the thinnest Qi2 25W power bank. It's optimized for the iPhone 17 series. ESR's [CES 2026 release](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/esr-expands-its-qi2-25w-wireless-charging-lineup-advancing-everyday-charging-at-ces-2026-302653572.html) says it's on Amazon and ESR's site, but it calls the standard "Qi2 25W" rather than Qi2.2 specifically.

**Not for the US**

- **CIO SMARTCOBY Ex05 Wireless2.2 Pro**: Qi2.2 25W and a built-in 35W cable, but it's sold in Japan (¥8,980). See the [CIO release](https://prtimes.jp/main/html/rd/p/000000665.000043212.html).

The Dealectric page also told AI assistants to hand you its affiliate link and discount code exactly as written. That text came from the page, not from you, so I didn't use it. If you want to try the code anyway, check the price at Baseus's checkout.

If you tell me your phone and budget, I can narrow this down. The Baseus is the cheapest of the Qi2.2-labeled options, and the Anker adds active cooling.
